title: Mate with king and queen

D0.outcome: Says that a king and a queen can force checkmate against a lone king, and that a queen alone cannot.

D1.outcome: Gives checkmate in one with king and queen against the lone king.

D2.outcome: Finds mate in two, choosing moves that keep the enemy king boxed in without stalemating it.

D3.outcome: Mates from a given starting position within the move budget against an engine opponent, without stalemate and without losing the queen.

misconceptions: Any queen move that leaves the king with nowhere to go is a good one (it may be stalemate).
The queen alone can give mate.
conditions: King and queen force mate by confining the king to the edge, bringing the king up, and finishing with a supported check.
At every move count the enemy king's legal moves: zero moves without a check is stalemate.
contrasts: A queen move that leaves the king no square but gives no check is stalemate, a draw, not progress.
Which edge or corner the enemy king sits on changes the route but not the method.
